newsitem.title: UK: British Telecom says results show health.
newsitem.headline: British Telecom says results show health.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc on Thursday posted second quarter and half-year results which chairman Sir Iain Vallance said showed the health of the firm in in the face of increasing competition and tough regulation.

BT, which plans to merge with MCI of the U.S. to create a global company, Concert, said profits before tax, redundancy and restructuring charges rose by 7.4 percent in the second quarter and by 5.2 percent in the first half.

Profits at the "headline' pre-tax level of 1.6 billion pounds ($2.64 billion) for the half year and 730 million pounds in the second quarter were flat on the same periods a year earlier, however, as redundancy charges in the half were 112 million pounds higher and BT also incurred a charge for the repurchase of government-held bonds.

"The results for the half year show an encouraging position with sustained high growth in demand for our telephony services and significant sales incrases in our new markets and advanced products," Vallance said in the results statement.

He said the figures, which included turnover in the six months up by 4.5 percent to 7.37 billion pounds, demonstrated that BT's business was well-positioned commercially and financially as it prepared to create Concert.

As previously announced, BT is raising its interim dividend by six percent to 7.9 pence. As part of the MCI deal, BT is also paying a special dividend of 35 pence which it expects to pay in September 1997 at the same time as the final dividend. ($1=.6054 Pound)
